input: The vectors printed on Meta's customer-information page (em John_Smith@gmail.com, fn Mary, fn Valery with accent, fn Korean name, country United States) run through hashed_user_data.
why: An advertiser's matched-event rate collapses if a Meta-documented value hashes differently than Meta expects, and nobody can see it. Measured: mismatching vectors: []. Code agrees.
promise: `em` trim and lowercase

input: Meta page phone vector as the relay needs it: '+1 (650) 555-1212'.
why: A US lead's phone would not match in Events Manager if the digits were mangled. Measured: got e323ec626319. Code agrees.
promise: `ph` digits only, leading zeros stripped

input: City and zip vectors from the same page (New York, Paris, AZ, 94035, GB 'M1 1AE').
why: Wrong city or zip normalisation silently lowers match quality for every lead. Measured: all five normalised forms equal the page's. Code agrees.
promise: `fn`, `ln`, `ct` lowercase, trim, strip punctuation and spaces for ct

input: A Philippine lead types '0917 123 4567' and the tenant has default_country_code 63.
why: A Philippine client's leads would never match on phone if the national zero were not swapped for 63. Measured: got 639171234567. Code agrees.
promise: `default_country_code` applied only to a number that starts with a single `0`

input: A lead types a US number without a plus or country code, '(415) 555-0100', no default configured.
why: A wrong phone hash is worse than none: it counts as a bad match. Measured: returned None. Code agrees.
promise: a number that still has no country code is OMITTED, not sent wrong

input: fbc from the Meta page example: fbclid IwAR2F4-dbP0l7Mn1IawQQGCINEz7PYXQvwjNwB_qa2ofrHyiLjcbCRxTDMgk, creation 1554763741205 ms.
why: A lowercased fbclid or seconds instead of milliseconds makes Meta ignore the click. Measured: fb.1.1554763741205.IwAR2F4-dbP0l7Mn1IawQ. Code agrees.
promise: fbclid case preserved exactly

input: A lead arrives with fbclid 'Iw AR?x=1' (a space and a query character).
why: Building an fbc from junk would send Meta a malformed cookie value for every such lead. Measured: fbc is None. Code agrees.
promise: fbclid case preserved exactly

input: An ad lead through /ingest to a CAPI sink: the unhashed ip, user agent, fbc stay as received and the fake accepts it.
why: If the relay hashed these four fields Meta would never match the user. Measured: effects=1 states=[('capi', 'done', None)]. Code agrees.
promise: NEVER hash `client_ip_address`, `client_user_agent`, `fbc`, `fbp`

input: The page URL carries ?email=pat%40example.com&phone=%2B14155550100 beside utm_source and fbclid.
why: Raw PII in event_source_url would be stored at Meta. Measured: https://shop.example.com/lp?utm_source=facebook&fbclid=IwAR2Ab_c-D. Code agrees.
promise: `event_source_url` keeps only `utm_*` and click-id query parameters

input: A funnel puts the lead's email in utm_term: ?utm_term=pat@example.com.
why: An email inside a UTM value would reach Meta in clear text. Measured: https://x.example/?utm_campaign=spring. Code agrees.
promise: UTM values are limited to 200 characters of letters, digits, space and `_ . - + % : /`

input: A page URL with userinfo and a fragment: https://bob:pw@shop.example.com:8443/a?x=1#frag.
why: Credentials or fragments sent to Meta. Measured: https://shop.example.com:8443/a. Code agrees.
promise: `event_source_url` keeps only `utm_*` and click-id query parameters

input: An ad lead arrives twice on /ingest with the same Idempotency-Key (HighLevel retry), CAPI and Slack enabled.
why: A retry must not double count a conversion at Meta or post twice. Measured: events=1 deliveries=2 meta=1 slack=1. Code agrees.
promise: A duplicate returns 200 and writes nothing.

input: A lead created 6 days 22 hours ago is delivered to CAPI.
why: Leads delayed by a relay outage must still reach Meta inside its 7 day window. Measured: effects=1 [('capi', 'done', None)]. Code agrees.
promise: an event 6 days 23 hours old is sent and an older one is `dead` with reason `older than 7 days`

input: A lead created 7 days 1 hour ago is delivered to CAPI.
why: Meta rejects the whole request; the relay must record dead with a reason instead of retrying. Measured: effects=0 [('capi', 'dead', 'older than 7 days')]. Code agrees.
promise: an event 6 days 23 hours old is sent and an older one is `dead` with reason `older than 7 days`

input: A ContactCreate with no click id and no allowlisted source (a manual import) on a default CAPI tenant.
why: An import must not be reported to Meta as an ad conversion. Measured: effects=0 [('capi', 'skipped', 'no click id (fbc, fbp, fbclid or an allowlisted source)')]. Code agrees.
promise: for a lead with none of `fbc`, `fbp`, `fbclid` or an allowlisted `source`

input: A tenant feeds CAPI only through the workflow Custom Webhook with the body the docs describe (event_key plus email, phone, fbclid, user_agent, page_url) and no type field.
why: Every such lead is skipped at Meta with no alert, and no doc tells the author to add type, so conversions silently never arrive. Measured: http 200; effects=0; [('capi', 'skipped', 'event type none is not mapped')]. Code DISAGREES.
promise: only the workflow path can produce website events

input: The same workflow body as the previous case with type set to Lead.
why: Positive control: proves the previous case fails only because of the missing type. Measured: effects=1 action_source=website. Code agrees.
promise: only the workflow path can produce website events

input: An OpportunityStatusUpdate won event on a tenant with no currency option.
why: A Purchase without currency is rejected by Meta, so it must be skipped with a reason. Measured: effects=0 [('capi', 'skipped', 'no currency')]. Code agrees.
promise: absent currency means `skipped` with reason `no currency`

input: A won opportunity delivered twice (two different Idempotency-Keys, same opportunity id) on a tenant with currency USD.
why: A re-won deal must not count twice at Meta. Measured: accepted effects=1 distinct event_ids=1 requests=2. Code agrees.
promise: Purchase `event_id` = `sha256(tenant|opportunity id|event_name)` so a re-won deal does not count twice

input: Meta answers 500 after it recorded the event (act_then_fail), then recovers.
why: A retry after an ambiguous failure must not create a second conversion. Measured: effects=1 [('capi', 'done', None)]. Code agrees.
promise: the fake's effect count is exactly 1 for CAPI and Sheets

input: Meta answers error 190 (token expired) for a lead.
why: The lead must wait (sink paused, alert) and not burn into dead rows. Measured: [('capi', 'pending', 'token rejected by Meta (http 400 code 190)')] paused=True. Code agrees.
promise: Outcomes 190, 410, 403 and Google `invalid_grant` PAUSE the sink for that tenant

input: Meta answers 429-style throttle (code 4) 50 times for 50 leads, then recovers.
why: Rate limits must not kill leads. Measured: done=50 effects=50. Code agrees.
promise: RETRY outcomes (429, queue full, throttle codes, timeouts, 5xx) do not increment `attempts`

input: Sheets answers 500 after the row landed, read-back works.
why: One lead must be one row. Measured: column A=['sh1'] [('sheets', 'done', None)]. Code agrees.
promise: the fake's effect count is exactly 1 for CAPI and Sheets

input: A lead whose name is '=HYPERLINK("http://x","a")' goes to Sheets.
why: A formula in a cell would run for whoever opens the sheet. Measured: text cells starting with '=': 1. Code agrees.
promise: RAW so a leading `=` stays text

input: An operator force-replays a DONE Sheets delivery (sink and force true) via /admin/replay.
why: The lead's row is appended a second time in the sales sheet. Measured: column A=['fr1', 'fr1']. Code DISAGREES.
promise: Sheets runs reconcile first

input: Sheets was down for 73 hours after the row landed, the delivery expired to dead, and the operator replays the dead row.
why: The documented recovery step duplicates a row that already exists. Measured: state before replay=dead; column A after replay=['dr1', 'dr1']. Code DISAGREES.
promise: Sheets runs reconcile first

input: A lead's free text answer is 10,000 characters full of & and <.
why: Slack refuses a section over 3000 characters and the lead would never be posted. Measured: effects=1 [('slack', 'done', None)]. Code agrees.
promise: truncated AFTER escaping to 2800 characters for Slack

input: A lead name contains a lone UTF-16 surrogate (an emoji cut in half by a form's character limit), delivered to Slack and Make.
why: The lead is never delivered to Make and is dead with a sink bug message; the person must be re-entered by hand. Measured: [('make', 'dead', 'sink bug: UnicodeEncodeError'), ('slack', 'done', None)]. Code DISAGREES.
promise: One bad lead never stops the loop

input: A worker is killed after Slack and Make accepted the call and before the result was saved; it restarts.
why: A crash must not lose a lead and may duplicate at most once. Measured: slack=2 make=2 [('make', 'done', None), ('slack', 'done', None)]. Code agrees.
promise: at most 2 and never 0 for Slack and Make

input: Two workers drain 30 leads at the same time against Slack.
why: A lead must not be posted twice because two workers claimed it. Measured: slack effects=30 (30 leads). Code agrees.
promise: overlapping workers never claim the same row

input: /ingest called with Idempotency-Key 'a' and body webhookId 'b'.
why: A mismatched key would dedupe the wrong events. Measured: http 400. Code agrees.
promise: when the body has `webhookId` it must equal the key, else 400

input: /hooks/acme/workflow with no event_key on a default tenant.
why: Two different leads with the same body would collapse into one. Measured: http 400 {'error': 'event_key-required: put a per-submission token in the workflow body as event_key', 'ok': False}. Code agrees.
promise: A workflow body with no `event_key` is rejected with 400

input: The same workflow event_key posted twice within a minute, then a third time 2 hours later.
why: A retry must dedupe; a later legitimate submission must not be dropped. Measured: dups=False,True,False events=2. Code agrees.
promise: Dedupe never drops a later legitimate event

input: A correctly signed direct delivery (signature over the raw bytes) is posted three times (HighLevel retries).
why: Retries must not create three leads. Measured: codes=[200, 200, 200] events=1. Code agrees.
promise: Accept a delivery when `X-GHL-Signature` verifies over the raw bytes OR over the compact re-serialisation

input: A delivery signed over the compact re-serialisation while the bytes sent were pretty printed.
why: HighLevel's own sample signs JSON.stringify(body); rejecting it would drop every lead. Measured: http 200. Code agrees.
promise: Accept a delivery when `X-GHL-Signature` verifies over the raw bytes OR over the compact re-serialisation

input: A forged signature (signed by another key) on a direct delivery.
why: A forged webhook must not create a lead. Measured: http 401 events=0. Code agrees.
promise: Verify `X-GHL-Signature` Ed25519 (base64) over the RAW bytes

input: A delivery carrying only the legacy X-WH-Signature header.
why: The retired scheme must fail closed. Measured: http 401. Code agrees.
promise: refuse a request that carries ONLY `X-WH-Signature` (fail closed)

input: A signed direct delivery whose body is 300 KB.
why: Oversize bodies are refused with 413 so memory cannot be exhausted. Measured: http 413. Code agrees.
promise: Cap request size at 256 KB (413)

input: Fathom delivers a signed meeting webhook three times with the same webhook-id.
why: Fathom retries must not post the meeting to Slack three times. Measured: codes=[200, 200, 200] slack=1 meetings=1. Code agrees.
promise: compared in constant time against EVERY space-delimited `v1,<b64>` entry

input: A webhook-signature header with a stale v1 entry first and the valid v1 entry second (secret rotation).
why: Rotation must not drop meetings. Measured: http 200. Code agrees.
promise: compared in constant time against EVERY space-delimited `v1,<b64>` entry

input: A Fathom webhook whose body was changed after signing.
why: A tampered meeting must not be stored. Measured: http 401. Code agrees.
promise: compared in constant time against EVERY space-delimited `v1,<b64>` entry

input: A correctly signed Fathom webhook with a timestamp 10 minutes old.
why: A replayed capture must be refused. Measured: http 401. Code agrees.
promise: timestamp within 5 minutes

input: A meeting stored from a webhook (with summary), then the daily puller runs with include_summary false and returns the same meeting.
why: The puller must not erase the summary the webhook stored. Measured: rows=1 summary=kept. Code agrees.
promise: Store `recording_id`, title, summary markdown and action items

input: An operator enables Sheets for a tenant that also receives Fathom meetings, then runs /admin/backfill for Sheets since the start.
why: The docs say only Slack ever gets a meeting, but a junk Sheets row (and a Make post of the summary) appears for each meeting. Measured: backfill inserted {'inserted': 1, 'ok': True}. Code DISAGREES.
promise: Store `recording_id`, title, summary markdown and action items; optional fan-out to Slack.

input: Meta Insights rows in USD '12.34', JPY '1500', KWD '12.345', string spend as the Insights edge returns them.
why: Wrong minor units misstate ad spend by 100x or 1000x. Measured: {'USD': True, 'JPY': True, 'KWD': True, 'KRW': True}. Code agrees.
promise: convert to integer minor units with an ISO 4217 exponent table (default 2, zero for JPY and KRW), never `float`

input: Windsor returns JSON numbers 1.15, 0.29, 4.35 and 1.005 for USD.
why: A float multiply gives 114, 28 or 434 cents. Measured: got [101, 435, 29, 115]. Code agrees.
promise: `Decimal(str(x))`

input: The 28 day re-pull sees Meta restate three days (10.00 to 11, 12, 13).
why: Restated spend must replace, never stack. Measured: rows=[1100, 1200, 1300]. Code agrees.
promise: Re-pull the last 28 days each run (data is stable after 28 days), upsert on the primary key.

input: Meta serves an empty first page that still carries paging.next.
why: Stopping at the empty page would leave the whole window unrecorded. Measured: rows=2. Code agrees.

input: Meta answers error 190 (token expired) on a pull that already has rows stored from yesterday.

input: Meta's paging.next points at another host.
why: Following it would hand the access token to that host. Measured: PullError: paging.next points away from the configured host and was not followed. Code agrees.

input: A Windsor pull that gets a 429 once, with the api_key in the URL.

promise: returning `matched`, `missing_in_ledger`, `missing_in_payments`, `amount_mismatch`, `duplicate`, `wrong_bucket`

input: A ledger CSV amount written as '1e3', another as '12.345' for USD, another as 'USD 5', another with an unknown currency 'XXQ'.
why: Silently misread money is worse than stopping. Measured: all four refused with CsvError. Code agrees.
